title: Embu Bean Stew
author: Mama Wanjiru

heritage.origin: Embu County — slopes of Mount Kenya, Eastern Kenya
heritage.history: The Embu are a Bantu community inhabiting the southeastern slopes of Mount Kenya. Their agricultural tradition is one of the most sophisticated in Kenya — the fertile volcanic soils have supported complex multi-crop farming for centuries. The Embu bean stew is a fundamental daily food, made from the community's own-grown beans.
heritage.modernEvolution: Embu bean stew continues as a daily food in the region. Locally grown Embu beans — particularly rosecoco and borlotti varieties — are exceptional.

desc: Embu Bean Stew — locally grown highland beans slow-simmered with onions, tomatoes, garlic, and simple spices into a thick, hearty stew. The traditional daily meal of the Embu people of Mount Kenya's southeastern slopes.
longDesc: The Embu bean stew reflects the philosophy of Mount Kenya's agricultural communities — the best ingredients need the simplest preparation. Locally grown beans simmered slowly produce a stew of natural depth that commercially grown beans cannot match.
ingredients: 400g dried beans — rosecoco, borlotti, or red kidney
steps: Cook in fresh water for 60—75 minutes until completely tender. Drain, reserving liquid.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden — 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomatoes, curry powder, and paprika. Cook for 8 minutes.
Add cooked beans and reserved liquid.
Simmer for 15—20 minutes until thick and well-combined.
chefTips: Rosecoco or borlotti beans have the best flavour.
The reserved bean cooking liquid is flavour-rich — use it.
The stew should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
cookingScience: Bean cooking liquid is rich in soluble fibre and plant protein that have leached from the beans. Using this liquid rather than fresh water adds body and flavour.
sustainabilityTips: Highland-grown Embu beans are sustainably produced on small farms with minimal inputs.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze for 3 months.
reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Rich in iron, folate, and potassium.
culturalNote: Embu bean stew embodies the agricultural wisdom of Mount Kenya's communities — generations of careful seed selection producing beans of exceptional quality.
